subject: Discovery follow-up: QuarryHealth technical fit, SLOs and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <agomez@quarryhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery follow-up: QuarryHealth technical fit, SLOs and next steps

Alex — great to meet this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of primary pain points you shared:
- High per-request latency spikes on document QA flows during morning batch processing windows (user-facing p95 spikes up to ~600ms today)
- Cost unpredictability from current multi-model routing and lack of KV caching for conversational context
- Compliance requirement: in-region data residency for PHI-related inference and audit logs retained 1 year

Goals you stated:
1) Reduce user-facing p95 latency to <= 150ms for short QA prompts (avg tokens ~80) under 95% of peak traffic
2) Target steady-state cost reduction of 30–40% vs current baseline by using batching + KV caching + a quantized model variant
3) Have a deployment plan that satisfies in-region hosting (us-west) and auditability for SOC2-like evidence

Technical notes / preliminary fit assessment (from our call):
- Model: recommended starting point is a 13B–16B open LLM with int8 quantization; requires 8k context for long-recall flows. We have verified variants that match the quality at quantized int8 op paths.
- Latency: to meet p95 <=150ms for short prompts we suggest a dedicated GPU pool (a mix of A100-style instances for KV-backed long sessions and T4-style for short stateless generation) with continuous batching tuned to 20–40ms target batch delay.
- Throughput: you mentioned bursts up to ~120 requests/s for the QA path — we mapped an initial capacity profile in the attached CSV.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for conversations should decrease token compute by ~25–35% for your workload; we recommend warm-warmed cache for peak hours and per-route TTLs.
- Fallbacks: can auto-fail to a smaller 7B variant (hosted) when Dedicated pool is saturated; will keep functionality while degrading cost/latency predictably.

Attachments I uploaded to the shared drive: qh-deploy-topology-v1.pdf (diagram + node counts), slo-latency-throughput-table.csv (capacity sketch).

Proposed next steps:
- Action A (this week): Lauren to run a quick capacity sketch with your published RPS / token distribution (Lauren, copied) — please share any telemetry you can (1 week window preferred).
- Action B (by Dec 10): Redwood to prepare a mutual action plan + cost estimate based on the capacity sketch and model choice.
- Action C: Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week with your infra team to validate network egress and KMS keys.

Can you confirm the telemetry window you can share and who from infra we should invite to the deep-dive?

Thanks — looking forward to progressing.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
[attachment: qh-deploy-topology-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

Ben — thanks for the concise recap, this matches our notes. A few clarifications and answers to your asks: 

Telemetry window: we can share the last 10 days of production traces and aggregated p95/p99 by route. We'll grant read-only access to a secure S3 bucket (procure@quarryhealth will send details).
Infra contacts for deep-dive: please invite Samir Patel (platform lead, samir.patel@quarryhealth.com) and Priya Menon (security, priya.menon@quarryhealth.com). Samir will want to validate TLS termination and latency added by our internal proxy.
PHI handling: we need explicit KMS envelope flow and audit logs captured in-region. SOC2 evidence is required as part of procurement — can you outline the logs we can expect (request/response hashes, audit trail points) before the deep-dive?
Model quality: we are running internal evals with a sampled prompt set; if you can share quantized model eval artifacts or a short checklist for quality gates that would help speed model selection.

Next steps on our side: procurement will outline an NDA + MSA path this week (procure@ will send for signature). We prefer the deep-dive on Mon Dec 7, 10:00–11:00 PT. Confirm availability?

Best,
Alex

Lauren — forwarding Alex's confirmations. Can you take the lead on the capacity sketch? Key inputs we have: burst 120 rps, avg tokens 80, long-pinned contexts (~20% of sessions require 4k+ context), retention/audit retention 1 year (PHI).

Please produce: 1) node sizing recommendation for US-WEST dedicated pool (min/target/max), 2) expected p95 latency projection with batching windows of 10/20/40ms, and 3) a short note on KMS integration patterns (customer-managed key options).

Target to have your sketch by EOD Friday so we can include cost estimates in Monday's deep-dive doc.

—Ben

Alex / Samir / Priya — thanks for confirming. Per Alex's ask, attaching two pre-reads and a short checklist we'll walk through in the deep-dive:
- qh-deploy-topology-v1.pdf (diagram: dedicated pool, cache layer, fallback routing)
- slo-latency-throughput-table.csv (capacity and p95 projections at different batching delays)

Pre-read checklist (we'll cover these live):
1) Network: TLS termination point, latency budget across your proxy, accepted egress CIDR for RW nodes
2) KMS: envelope encryption options (customer-managed KMS in us-west), key rotation cadence
3) Logging: request/response metadata we produce (timestamps, model id, token counts, request hash) and retention options
4) Failover: model variant routing and expected degradation profile for 7B fallback
5) Ops: canary plan + rollback windows for model rollouts

If you want any additional telemetry added to the capacity sketch before Monday, shoot the file share link and Lauren will pull it in. Meeting invite sent.

Talk Monday —
Ben
